preconditions.description: The number of objects n is between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= type_i <= 1 for type_i in type_list)
preconditions.description: Each object type is either 0 (mountain) or 1 (hotel).
At least one object is a hotel.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= a_i <= n for a_i in a_list)
preconditions.description: Each a_i is either 0 (no incoming track) or a valid object index (1 to n).
The input lists type_list and a_list have exactly n elements each.

postconditions.description: The first line of stdout is the integer k (path length), followed by k integers representing the path.
The path length k is at least 1.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(v) <= n for v in path)
postconditions.description: All objects in the path are valid indices between 1 and n.

postconditions.expression: all(type_list[int(v) - 1] == 0 for v in path[:-1]) and type_list[int(path[-1]) - 1] == 1
postconditions.description: All objects in the path except the last are mountains, and the last object is a hotel.

postconditions.expression: all(int(path[i]) + 1 == int(path[i + 1]) for i in range(len(path) - 1))
postconditions.description: Each consecutive pair of objects in the path satisfies v_{i+1} = v_i + 1.

postconditions.expression: all(a_list[int(path[i]) - 1] == int(path[i - 1]) if i > 0 else True for i in range(1, len(path)))
postconditions.description: For each object v_i in the path (i > 1), there is exactly one incoming ski track from v_{i-1}.

postconditions.expression: not any(k2 > k for k2, path2 in [line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]] if len(path2) == k2 and all(type_list[int(v) - 1] == 0 for v in path2[:-1]) and type_list[int(path2[-1]) - 1] == 1 and all(int(path2[i]) + 1 == int(path2[i + 1]) for i in range(len(path2) - 1)))
postconditions.description: The path length k is maximal among all valid paths.
